title: Release audit: `forgel_code/interactive.py`'s `redact()` does not keep key material out of the
summary: Replace `redact()` with a structured redactor that recognizes separators (`:`, `=`, whitespace), auth schemes such as `Bearer`, quoted values, Russian secret labels, environment-variable names and generic key material, and redacts the entire value rather than only the next token. Add direct tests for `token:abc123`, `Authorization: Bearer abc123`, `токен: abc123`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=abc` and an engine reply containing such text.
requirements: Masking means: for a recognized secret-bearing label, the value bound to that label is replaced by a single fixed mask marker while the label is preserved, so the original value does not appear anywhere in the displayed text.
A value following a recognized secret keyword and a colon, with or without intervening whitespace, is masked.
A value following a recognized secret keyword and an equals sign, with or without surrounding whitespace, is masked.
A value following a recognized secret keyword and whitespace (the previously supported single-token form) continues to be masked.
A value that follows a recognized secret keyword plus a colon or whitespace and then an authorization scheme word is masked; the scheme word may remain visible, the credential after it may not.
Secret keywords are recognized in English and in Russian; a Russian secret label followed by a colon, an equals sign or whitespace masks its value exactly as an English label does.
A compound label containing a secret keyword as one of its segments is treated as a secret-bearing label; the whole label may remain visible but its bound value is masked.
Label recognition is case-insensitive, including for non-English labels.
Text not bound to a recognized secret-bearing label is displayed unchanged, including ordinary sentences that merely contain the word for a secret without a bound value.
The label text itself is preserved next to the mask so the user can tell what kind of value was hidden.
Masking is applied to every engine reply and every engine error before it is shown in the session, with no path by which engine output reaches the screen unmasked.
Masking already-masked text neither errors nor reveals a value, and masking empty or secret-free text returns it unchanged.
Previously working session behavior continues to work, including the masking forms that already worked.
acceptance: A message containing a secret label followed directly by a colon and a value is displayed with the value replaced by the mask marker and the value absent from the displayed text.

A message containing a secret label, a colon, an authorization scheme word and a credential is displayed with the label and surrounding wording preserved and the credential replaced by the mask marker.
A message containing a Russian secret label followed by a colon and a value is displayed with the value replaced by the mask marker.
A message containing a compound label built from several segments, one of which is a secret keyword, joined to a value is displayed with the value replaced by the mask marker.
A message containing a secret label joined to a value by an equals sign with no surrounding spaces is displayed with the value replaced by the mask marker.
A message that merely mentions a secret word without binding a value to it is displayed unchanged.
A message with no secret-bearing label is displayed byte-for-byte unchanged, including punctuation, spacing and wording.
Masking the same message twice produces the same displayed result as masking it once, and masking empty text succeeds and yields empty text.
Every engine reply and every engine error that reaches the session display is masked under these rules, with no displayed engine text bypassing masking.
For each recognized form above, the secret value does not appear as a substring anywhere in what the user is shown for that message.
Previously working session behavior does not regress.
plan_goal: Forgel Code: interactive agent client instead of a command wrapper

checks.criterion: Separator-bound values are masked whole: 'token:abc123' shows 'token:[redacted]', 'password: hunter2' shows 'password: [redacted]', 'password = hunter2' shows 'password = [redacted]', and 'password==hunter2' shows 'password==[redacted]'.

An authorization scheme stays visible and its credential is masked: 'Authorization: Bearer abc123' shows 'Authorization: Bearer [redacted]' and 'the token Bearer secretvalue' shows 'the token Bearer [redacted]'.

Russian and compound labels are masked: 'токен: abc123' shows 'токен: [redacted]', 'AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=abc' shows 'AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=[redacted]', and 'пароль: hunter2', 'db_password=hunter2', 'aws.secret.key: hunter2' and 'api-key=hunter2' each show their value as [redacted].

Benign prose is displayed byte-for-byte unchanged: 'Password updated.' and 'Secret rotation scheduled' come back identical, and so do 'the token is missing', 'rotate the password please', 'send the secret later', 'release: 0.1.1 open', an empty message and 'нажмите на кнопку (дважды)!'.

A bare label followed by a word that is not recognised everyday prose is masked wherever the label sits: 'token abc' shows 'token [redacted]', 'токен abc123' shows 'токен [redacted]', 'the token abc' shows 'the token [redacted]', and 'set password swordfish' shows 'set password [redacted]'.
A quoted value is masked whole with its quotation marks visible: 'password: "hunter2 and more"' shows 'password: "[redacted]"'.
Masking is idempotent: masking already-masked text returns it unchanged, and each masked result carries exactly one marker per masked value.

An engine reply, a task title and an engine error that contain a bound value reach the screen masked; a reply containing 'токен: abc123' and 'Authorization: Bearer abc123' shows neither value fragment anywhere in the session output.
No other behaviour changes: every behaviour that worked before this change still works afterwards.

external_dependencies.name: Forgel engine command line
external_dependencies.interface: The client starts it as a subprocess with an operation name and reads one JSON object from its standard output, with error text on its standard error; the engine lives in another project and is simulated for the client's own examples.

result.summary: Addressed the remaining review failures on top of the previous attempt. `redact()` in `forgel_code/interactive.py` now separates a bound value from ordinary prose with one stated rule: a label binds the following word unless that word is recognised everyday prose (a fixed vocabulary of English/Russian function words plus ordinary narrative verbs and nouns such as 'updated' or 'rotation') that carries no key-material markers (digits, mixed case, value punctuation). Consequently a clause-initial or mid-sentence benign mention (`Password updated.`, `Secret rotation scheduled`, `the token is missing`) is displayed byte-for-byte unchanged, while the previously working whitespace form is masked wherever the label sits (`the token abc`, `set password swordfish`, `установлен пароль swordfish`). Colon/equals forms (including `==` and spaced `=`), authorization schemes (`Authorization: Bearer abc123`, `the token Bearer secretvalue`), Russian stem labels, compound/environment labels, quoted values (including unclosed quotes hiding the rest of the line) and copula forms (`the token is VALUE`) keep masking only the value. The prose exemption is applied after the scheme, copula, quote and separator branches so no masking form regressed; masking stays idempotent and total for empty text, and every engine reply, error and state line still passes through the single `write()` funnel that calls `redact()`. `tests/test_redact.py` was rewritten around the new specification: each acceptance criterion has an executable example, including the two previously failing directions (`Password updated.`/`Secret rotation scheduled` unchanged; `the token abc`/`set password swordfish` masked), a byte-for-byte check for secret-free text, idempotence, absence of the value as a substring, and session-level checks that an engine reply containing `токен: abc123` and `Authorization: Bearer abc123`, a task title carrying `password=hunter2`, and an engine error carrying `password: hunter2` all reach the screen masked. Verification: `python -m pytest -q tests/test_redact.py` (12 passed, 17 subtests), `python -m pytest -q tests/test_interactive.py` (37 passed, 10 subtests), and the full suite `python -m pytest -q` (267 passed, 172 subtests).
assumptions: The prose vocabulary is finite and maintained in the client: the words that make the named benign examples benign are members, and 'abc', 'swordfish' and 'hunter2' are not, matching the specification's prose-vocabulary rule.
A word recognised as prose is compared case-insensitively after stripping quotes and trailing sentence punctuation, so 'updated.' in 'Password updated.' still counts as prose.
The separator branches (':', '=') remain unconditional, so 'Secret: rotation' masks while 'Secret rotation scheduled' does not, as the specification's assumptions state.
The quoted-run rule covers " ' ` and « »; an unclosed quote masks to the end of its line.
No documentation file needed a change: the specification already states the behaviour implemented.

checks.criterion: A message containing a secret label followed directly by a colon and a value is displayed with the value replaced by the mask marker and the value absent from the displayed text.
Previously working session behavior does not regress.
Every engine reply and every engine error that reaches the session display is masked under these rules, with no displayed engine text bypassing masking.

review.summary: The change rewrites `redact()` into a label/binding parser that covers colon-, equals-, scheme-, Russian- and compound-label forms, and it adds `tests/test_redact.py` including session-level checks that replies, engine state and engine errors are masked before display. However, the prose/credential heuristics the implementation introduces break two opposing requirements. First, a clause-initial secret word followed by an ordinary word is treated as a bound value, so benign text such as `Password updated.` or `Secret rotation scheduled` is altered, which contradicts the requirement that text merely mentioning a secret word is displayed unchanged. Second, the previously working whitespace form is now gated on the label starting a clause or the value looking credential-like, so a mid-sentence form such as `the token abc` or `set password swordfish` is no longer masked, regressing the previously supported behavior and leaving the secret visible. The tests only cover the forms that happen to pass, so neither defect is caught.

requirements.requirement: FR-1: a bound value is replaced by one fixed mask marker while the label is preserved.
requirements.note: The rewritten `redact()` splices `[redacted]` over the bound span and keeps the label text; the tests confirm the label stays next to the mask.

requirements.requirement: FR-2: a value after a secret keyword and a colon, with or without whitespace, is masked.
requirements.note: Covered by `test_a_colon_joined_value_is_masked`; the `:` branch in `_binding` does not depend on surrounding prose.

requirements.requirement: FR-3: a value after a secret keyword and an equals sign, with or without surrounding whitespace, is masked.
requirements.note: Covered by `test_an_equals_joined_value_is_masked` and by the compound-label cases.

requirements.requirement: FR-4: a value after a recognized secret keyword and whitespace (the previously supported single-token form) continues to be masked.
requirements.note: The whitespace branch requires the label to stand alone or the next word to look credential-like (`_stands_alone` / `_looks_like_credential`). `the token abc`, `set password swordfish` or `установлен пароль swordfish` therefore stay unmasked, although the previous implementation masked the following token in any position.

requirements.requirement: FR-5: a value after a secret keyword plus colon or whitespace and an authorization scheme word is masked, scheme word may stay.
FR-6: English and Russian secret labels are recognized for colon, equals and whitespace forms.
requirements.note: Russian stems are matched case-insensitively and the colon/equals cases pass; the whitespace Russian case shares the FR-4 defect and is reported there.

requirements.requirement: FR-7: a compound label with a secret keyword as one segment has its value masked.
requirements.note: `_segments`/`_secret_label` handle `_`, `.` and `-`, and the compound cases in `test_a_compound_label_is_masked` pass.

requirements.requirement: FR-8: label recognition is case-insensitive, including non-English labels.
requirements.note: Labels are lower-cased before matching; `Пароль=hunter2` is masked.

requirements.requirement: FR-9: text not bound to a recognized secret-bearing label is displayed unchanged, including ordinary sentences that merely mention a secret word.
requirements.note: A clause-initial label followed by any word that is not in the prose list is treated as bound: `Password updated.` becomes `Password [redacted].` and `Secret rotation scheduled` is altered. That is an ordinary sentence mentioning the label without a value, and it violates this requirement.

requirements.requirement: FR-10: the label text is preserved next to the mask.
requirements.note: The label span is never replaced; only the value span is.

requirements.requirement: FR-11/AC-9 (review-only): every engine reply and every engine error is masked before it reaches the session display.
requirements.note: The attributed session tests exercise the reply path, the engine-state path and the error path and assert the values are absent and `[redacted]` is present; the diff does not remove any display-side redaction call.

requirements.requirement: FR-12: masking empty or secret-free text returns it unchanged and masking twice neither errors nor reveals a value.
requirements.note: `redact('')` returns early, `_span` recognizes an existing `[redacted]` span, and `test_redaction_is_idempotent`/`test_secret_free_text_is_unchanged` pass.

requirements.requirement: FR-13: previously working session behavior, including the masking forms that already worked, does not regress.
requirements.note: The old implementation masked the token following a secret keyword anywhere in the text; the new standalone/credential heuristic drops that for mid-sentence occurrences, so a previously masked form now leaks.

requirements.requirement: AC-6: a message that merely mentions a secret word without binding a value is displayed unchanged.
requirements.note: Only the three chosen sample sentences are tested; `Password updated.` is a counterexample that is masked.

requirements.requirement: AC-7: a message with no secret-bearing label is displayed byte-for-byte unchanged.
requirements.note: Messages with no secret at all are preserved, but the requirement is contradicted for ordinary messages mentioning a label: `Token expired` is rewritten to `Token [redacted]`.

requirements.requirement: AC-10: for each recognized form the secret value does not appear as a substring of what the user is shown.
requirements.note: The whitespace-joined form leaks when it appears mid-sentence and the value is short and alphabetic, e.g. `the token abc` is displayed unchanged.

blocking: FR-9/AC-6/AC-7: a clause-initial secret label followed by an ordinary word is masked as if bound, so benign text such as `Password updated.` or `Secret rotation scheduled` is altered instead of displayed unchanged.

FR-4/FR-13/AC-10: the previously working whitespace form is no longer masked mid-sentence when the value is short and alphabetic (e.g. `the token abc`, `set password swordfish`), so the secret remains visible.

feedback:
The specification was rewritten after an invalid check: … [truncated]
defines what distinguishes a bound value from prose. The rewrite must decide and state that distinction (for example: the whitespace form masks only a token that carries key-material markers such as digits, mixed case or value punctuation, while an ordinary word is left visible; and the previously supported whitespace form keeps masking regardless of where in the sentence the label appears), and must then make the acceptance criteria agree with that decision in both directions — a benign sentence such as `Password updated.` or `Secret rotation scheduled` displayed byte-for-byte unchanged, and a mid-sentence form such as `the token abc` or `set password swordfish` displayed with the value masked — so every listed form has one and only one expected outcome and no implementation has to guess.
Implement the new specification. Do not change code only to satisfy the old check.

last_failure.message: FR-4 and FR-9 are contradictory as written: both cover a secret label followed by whitespace and a single ordinary word, FR-4 requiring the word to be masked as a bound value and FR-9 requiring the message to be displayed unchanged, and the specification never defines what distinguishes a bound value from prose. The rewrite must decide and state that distinction (for example: the whitespace form masks only a token that carries key-material markers such as digits, mixed case or value punctuation, while an ordinary word is left visible; and the previously supported whitespace form keeps masking regardless of where in the sentence the label appears), and must then make the acceptance criteria agree with that decision in both directions — a benign sentence such as `Password updated.` or `Secret rotation scheduled` displayed byte-for-byte unchanged, and a mid-sentence form such as `the token abc` or `set password swordfish` displayed with the value masked — so every listed form has one and only one expected outcome and no implementation has to guess.
